mathematical_proof.method: Represent a regular octahedron by vertices +/-e1,+/-e2,+/-e3, up to irrelevant uniform scale. A face has one vertex from each opposite pair. Adjacent faces sharing an edge must have antipodal third vertices. The connected net therefore fixes all vertex identities from any seed face, up to a global symmetry.
mathematical_proof.human_readable_conclusion: With seed (n0,n1,n2)=(e1,e2,e3), propagation gives n3=-e2, n4=-e1, n5=e2, n6=-e3, n7=e1, n8=-e2, n9=-e1. Thus x=n8-n9 has endpoints {-e2,-e1}, and E=n3-n4 has exactly those endpoints. A=n7-n8 and D=n0-n3 have {e1,-e2}; B=n5-n7 and C=n0-n1 have {e1,e2}. E is the only labelled match. In particular, n7 and n9 are antipodal, not coincident: the common planar endpoint n8 of A and x does not make their other endpoints glue. At n8 the two distinct folded red-edge rays have a 90-degree angle, not zero. Global rotation/reflection changes no edge coincidence.
